papers.title_en: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
papers.authors: Baihan Yang, Xin Lin, Yufan Wei, Baiang Li, Yuheng Liu, Juanxi Tian, Xiaohui Xie, Truong Nguyen
papers.evidence: 基于扩散Transformer的高保真图像抠图
papers.tldr: 现有图像抠图多依赖潜空间扩散模型，VAE压缩与重建会损失高频细节，难以满足高精度alpha需求。PixelMatte将预训练像素空间扩散Transformer用于抠图，复用原生patch embedding把图像、trimap与噪声alpha作为空间对齐token联合处理，实现单次前向像素级预测。方法结合合成监督、真实图像微调及LayerShift与High-Pass Refiner校准，在四个基准和两种骨干上显著降低SAD与梯度误差。结果表明像素空间生成先验对精度敏感抠图有效。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining. However, existing approaches largely rely on latent diffusion models, whose compressed representations and VAE-based reconstruction introduce a mismatch with the high-frequency precision required for matting. We present PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for high-fidelity image matting. We show that strong image-conditioned matting capabilities can be acquired even from a pure text-to-image model without paired image-to-image pretraining. Our approach reuses the backbone's native patch embedding to jointly process the input image, trimap, and noisy alpha matte as spatially aligned tokens, enabling direct pixel-space prediction without additional condition encoders or adapters. With pixel-accurate synthetic supervision and real-image fine-tuning, PixelMatte predicts alpha mattes in a single forward pass. Two lightweight calibration modules, LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner, further improve regional opacity accuracy and boundary fidelity. Experiments across four benchmarks and two distinct pixel diffusion backbones demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods, reducing SAD and gradient errors by 24-44% relative to RenderMatte on P3M-500-NP and AM-2K, while achieving competitive performance on AIM-500 and RenderMatte-2K. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of pixel-space generative priors for precision-sensitive image matting. Project page: https://white-yc.github.io/pixelmatte/.

papers.title_en: X-Matte: VAE-Free Pixel-Space Flow Matching for Single-Step Image Matting
papers.authors: Zanyi Wang, Jiaang Li, Dengyang Jiang, Ziru Wang, Chengzu Li, Davit Abrahamyan, Harry Yang, Serge Belongie, Mengmeng Wang
papers.evidence: 无需VAE的单步图像抠图并保留精细alpha细节
papers.tldr: 现有基于预训练生成先验的抠图方法多依赖VAE，潜空间压缩容易损失alpha边缘细节，并带来额外编解码与迭代采样开销。X-Matte取消潜空间压缩，将RGB到alpha的转换直接建模为像素空间连续流，并用轨迹级x-prediction和过渡感知alpha监督，使模型从中间状态学习并单次前向预测目标alpha。在P3M无trimap基准上，其表现与当前先进方法相当，还能零样本泛化到RWP-636和AIM-500。高分辨率下相较构造的单步潜空间对照最高实现9.4倍推理加速，说明无VAE像素空间流匹配可兼顾精细抠图与高效推理。
papers.abstract_en: Pre-trained generative models offer rich visual priors for image matting, but their adaptation often relies on variational autoencoders (VAEs), whose spatial compression can degrade fine alpha details and introduce additional inference overhead. To address these limitations, we propose X-Matte, a VAE-free pixel-space flow matching framework for single-step image matting. By eliminating latent compression, X-Matte formulates the RGB-to-alpha transition as a continuous flow directly in pixel space. We adopt trajectory-wide x-prediction with transition-aware alpha supervision, enabling the model to learn from intermediate states while directly predicting the target alpha matte in a single forward pass. This design avoids both VAE encoding and decoding and iterative sampling. Extensive experiments demonstrate performance competitive with state-of-the-art trimap-free matting methods on P3M benchmarks, together with promising zero-shot generalization to RWP-636 and AIM-500. Moreover, X-Matte achieves up to a 9.4x inference speedup over a constructed single-step latent counterpart at high resolution, demonstrating the effectiveness of VAE-free pixel-space modeling for accurate and efficient image matting.

papers.title_en: CIRKDV2: Cross-Image Relational Knowledge Distillation with Contextual Modeling for Efficient Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors: Chuanguang Yang, Yu Wang, Chengqing Yu, Xinqiang Yu, Weilun Feng, Yuqi Li, Zhulin An, Libo Huang, Boyu Diao, Fei Wang, Fuzhen Zhuang, Yongjun Xu, Yingli Tian, Tingwen Huang, Yongduan Song
papers.evidence: 面向高效语义分割的跨图像关系知识蒸馏
papers.tldr: 现有语义分割知识蒸馏多让学生模仿单图结构信息，忽视数据集中跨图像的全局语义关系。CIRKDV2将教师从全局图像建模的像素-像素、像素-区域和通道-通道关系迁移给学生，并用上下文聚合增强学生像素嵌入以缓解师生语义鸿沟。在Cityscapes、ADE20K、Pascal VOC和COCO-Stuff-164K上，该方法跨多种网络架构大幅超越现有分割蒸馏方法。其贡献在于结合跨图像关系蒸馏与上下文特征蒸馏，提升高效分割学生的特征表征能力。
papers.abstract_en: Existing Knowledge Distillation (KD) methods for semantic segmentation often guide the student to mimic the teacher's structured information generated from an individual image. However, they ignore the global semantic relations across various images that are valuable for KD. This paper proposes Cross-Image Relational KD V2 (CIRKDV2), which focuses on transferring structured pixel-to-pixel, pixel-to-region, and channel-to-channel relations modeled from global images in the dataset. A large teacher network often constructs a well-structured feature space in terms of global contextual dependencies. CIRKDV2 makes the student mimic the better structured semantic relations of the teacher, thus improving the feature representational capability. Beyond relational distillation, we further propose contextual feature distillation by using context aggregation to augment student pixel embeddings to match the semantic level with the teacher. This avoids the semantic gap problem between the teacher and student occurred in traditional feature distillation studies. Experimental results on Cityscapes, ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and COCO-Stuff-164K demonstrate that CIRKDV2 outperforms the state-of-the-art semantic segmentation distillation methods by large margins across various network architectures. Our code and pre-trained models are publicly available at https://github.com/winycg/CIRKD.

papers.title_en: ReSA: Preserving Reference-Specified Foreground in In-Context Segmentation
papers.authors: Dezhao Su, Bingxu Hou, Jingdi Lei, Lin Qian, Likai Wang, Yunyun Wan
papers.evidence: 参考引导的上下文分割，保持指定前景与边界
papers.tldr: 上下文分割需用参考图指定查询图中的目标前景，但现有方法易引入无关预测、前景保留不足。ReSA 以共享参考核统一查询自适应与掩码选择：用前景/背景原型约束自适应中的预测变化，并通过参考加权重建引导前景选择，同时按选定前景阈值对齐边界细化。方法冻结视觉编码器、仅做轻量测试时自适应，无需离线任务训练。在十个对象、部件及跨域基准上平均 mIoU 最高，1-shot 62.6%、5-shot 71.8%。
papers.abstract_en: In-context segmentation uses annotated references to specify the target and its extent in a query image. Accurately transferring this reference-specified foreground requires recovering target regions while suppressing irrelevant predictions. We propose ReSA, a reference-guided framework that unifies query adaptation and mask selection through a shared reference kernel. ReSA leverages foreground and background reference prototypes to constrain prediction changes during adaptation and guide foreground selection through reference-weighted reconstruction. This shared guidance promotes consistent use of reference information across prediction refinement and mask formation. ReSA further selects among adapted predictions and aligns boundary refinement with the selected foreground threshold. We establish a theoretical bound connecting reference-response changes during adaptation and soft reconstruction. With a frozen visual encoder and lightweight test-time adaptation, ReSA requires no offline task training. Ablation studies demonstrate improved foreground retention and effective suppression of false-positive regions, while qualitative results show more complete masks with fewer isolated artifacts. Across ten object, part, and cross-domain segmentation benchmarks, ReSA achieves the highest average mIoU among the evaluated methods, reaching 62.6% in 1-shot and 71.8% in 5-shot.

papers.title_en: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
papers.authors: Yu Chen, Haosen Yang, Su Ee Tan, Zhensong Zhang, Jifei Song, Jiankang Deng
papers.evidence: 面向单目深度基础模型的开放评测基准
papers.tldr: 3D感知正从任务专用转向几何基础模型，但现有评测因采样、分辨率、划分不同而不可比，且对齐方式会显著影响误差。作者提出 SpatialArena，统一指标与规则，覆盖五类任务、23个公开数据集和自采数据，采用稳健确定性对齐。评测52个模型发现单图深度在公开基准接近饱和但在大范围非受控场景仍不足，进展来自跨帧跨视角一致性。贡献是公开基准、工具箱与榜单。
papers.abstract_en: 3D perception is shifting from task-specific pipelines to geometric foundation models: monocular depth networks, feed-forward 3D/4D reconstruction models, and vision--language models that predict geometry. However, their progress cannot be measured reliably. Published numbers are not comparable, because every paper samples frames, sets resolutions, and selects test splits differently. They are not robust because the alignment required for every up-to-scale prediction can outweigh the gap between models: fitting depth in the wrong space nearly triples its error, and standard trajectory alignment understates the error of failing methods by up to $2.6\times$. And they rarely cover long recordings, dynamic scenes, or aerial views. We present SpatialArena, an open arena that scores geometric models with the same metrics and rules, with robust and deterministic alignment. SpatialArena spans five tasks, from monocular depth to SLAM. It covers 23 public datasets with 418,929 images across indoor, outdoor, aerial, object-centric, and dynamic scenes, together with Spatial Arena, our own captures with accurate poses and depth. Evaluating 52 models, we find that single-image depth is close to saturation on public benchmarks but not on large, uncontrolled scenes, and that progress now comes from consistency across frames and views, where feed-forward 3D/4D models match or surpass monocular specialists and overtake video depth models. The benchmark, toolbox, and leaderboard will be publicly released.

papers.title_en: SPiXSeg: Rethinking MLLM-based Image Segmentation as Superpixel Classification
papers.authors: Piyush Tiwary, Sohini Dutta, Prathosh A. P
papers.evidence: 基于多模态大模型的开放词汇图像分割，用超像素分类提升前景背景边界精度
papers.tldr: 现有MLLM图像分割依赖解码器或patch预测，边界精度与决策数量难兼顾，自回归掩码还带来顺序解码开销。SPiXSeg改为超像素级标签分配：现成模型一次性划分任务无关超像素，聚合patch特征为token，S2M在单次前向中比较隐藏表示打分，无需自回归或独立评分网络。RefCOCO系列平均cIoU达80.5/81.9；仅用COCO-Stuff训练也能开放词汇分割，ADE20K、PASCAL Context、VOC的mIoU为29.0、59.5、95.4。结果表明固定、查询无关超像素划分足以支持准确语言引导分割。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are widely used for image segmentation. However, existing methods either use a decoder or use patch-based approach which trades boundary precision against the number of decisions as coarse grid cells mix foreground and background pixels, while finer grids require many more predictions, and autoregressive mask generation adds sequential decoding overhead. We propose SPiXSeg, which shifts the output from per-patch to per-superpixel label assignment, using superpixel tokens formed by aggregating patch-level visual features. An off-the-shelf model partitions each image into task-agnostic superpixels, so the partition is computed once and reused across tasks. A Spix-to-Mask (S2M) module scores each superpixel token in a single MLLM forward pass by directly comparing the MLLM's hidden representations, without autoregressive generation or a separate scoring network, and the selected superpixels are mapped directly to pixels without refinement. Without any trainable decoder head or post-hoc refinement, SPiXSeg achieves an average cIoU of 80.5 with LLaVA-1.5-7B and 81.9 with InternVL2.5-8B on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg and, when trained only on COCO-Stuff, extends to open-vocabulary semantic segmentation with mIoU of 29.0, 59.5 and 95.4 on ADE20K, PASCAL Context and PASCAL VOC, outperforming several SoTA MLLM baselines. Our results suggest that a fixed, query-agnostic superpixel partition is enough for accurate language-guided segmentation.
